claims.text: Replacing an EAM reference with a deep neural-network potential will improve phase-space overlap with the ab initio liquid.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch near melting.
A deep-learning potential can be used to represent multicomponent high-entropy materials in both solid and liquid states.
Training on extensive ab initio data can capture the full spectrum of atomic configurations in the liquid phase.
The proposed approach applies to equimolar or near-equimolar high-entropy carbonitrides and solid-solution HEAs.
The applicable near-melting temperature range is approximately 3000–3600 K.
A high-entropy carbonitride composition has a reported melting-temperature maximum of 3580 ± 30 K.
A deep-learning potential can represent local atomic arrangements in high-entropy carbonitride liquids sufficiently to analyze pair correlations and structural changes.
The deep-learning potential represents local arrangements and short-range order more accurately than a conventional EAM reference.
Deep-learning potentials provide more comprehensive sampling of the ab initio liquid configuration space than EAM potentials.
More comprehensive liquid sampling reduces configuration-space mismatch relative to an EAM reference.
Reduced configuration-space mismatch produces a smoother free-energy integration path than TOR-TILD with traditional EAM references.
The intervention may approximately halve the thermodynamic-integration path error.
Reducing integration-path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy estimates.
TOR-TILD EAM references are unable to capture the large set of configurations present in ab initio liquid simulations.
The improvement should be larger in multicomponent high-entropy alloys than in elemental or binary systems.
RDFs and coordination-number distributions can serve as indicators of target–reference phase-space overlap.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant reduction exceeding 20% in integration-path mismatch, together with failure to improve phase-space overlap, would falsify the hypothesis.
